findings.body: The name is resolved from the raw lines aggregated into each result row, but `rowLabels` is keyed only by the raw GL/leaf value. Existing selections may contain multiple dimensions, and production SQL groups by every selected dimension (`backend/src/sql/sqlBuilder.ts:62-68,118-119`); `gl_code` plus `month` is an exercised shape (`backend/src/warehouse/measure-filter.db.test.ts:95-98`). Two month rows can therefore share a GL key while their month-scoped name counts select different primary names. A key-only client join cannot identify which label belongs to which row. Use a full row identity/index, or define one label per key over the whole answer scope.
findings.title: Key per-row labels by a unique row identity

findings.body: Supported answers allow any time window with the line dimension and an authorized Actual, but the context unconditionally requires a last-month budget batch and outline. The existing statement projection deliberately emits actual-only rows through a full outer join and leaves `budget_batch_id` null when there is no budget side (`backend/src/sql/sqlBuilder.ts:269-294`). Thus an otherwise supported Actual answer can exist without the required batch, making its drill context impossible to construct. Either exclude this shape explicitly or permit an absent budget pin/outline while retaining the executed query's bound triples, and cover that outcome in C8.
findings.title: Define drilling when the last month has no budget batch
